idea: A retired lighthouse keeper sits by a rain-streaked window at dusk, turning an old brass key in his fingers. He says: "Forty-one years I climbed those stairs, every single night, through every storm, and not one ship went down while I was keeping the light." Then he looks out at the dark sea and adds quietly: "Now a computer does it, and nobody remembers my name, but on quiet nights I still wake up at three and check the sky."

script.title: The Keeper's Watch
script.logline: A retired lighthouse keeper turns an old brass key by a rainy window, reminiscing on decades of keeping ships safe from the rocks.
script.setting: A dimly lit coastal cottage room by a rain-streaked window overlooking a stormy ocean at dusk.

characters.name: Arthur
characters.look: A seventy-year-old man with deep weathered facial wrinkles, wild sea-salted grey hair, a thick salt-and-pepper beard, wearing a frayed navy wool cable-knit sweater, with a faded blue anchor tattoo on his left cheekbone.
characters.voiceDescription: Gravelly low male voice, early 70s, coastal New England accent, slow and wistful.

shots.visual: Arthur twirls a tarnished heavy brass key between his scarred knuckles, the blue dusk and rain reflections gleaming against his weathered face.
shots.motion: Arthur slowly turns the key over his thumb, his jaw tightening with solemn pride as he speaks directly toward the room.
shots.line: Forty-one years I climbed those stairs, every single night, through every storm, and not one ship went down while I was keeping the light.
shots.speaker: Arthur

shots.visual: Arthur turns his head to gaze through the rain-streaked windowpane out at the dark distant ocean, a faint sweep of artificial light catching his eyes.
shots.motion: Arthur grips the key tightly into his palm and lowers his chin slightly, speaking in a subdued, reflective whisper.
shots.line: Now a computer does it, and nobody remembers my name, but on quiet nights I still wake up at three and check the sky.
shots.speaker: Arthur
